claims.text: Eon's production assistant (Eon Buzz, reported 26 August 2026) moved triage, semantic-layer and tenant-provided specialists behind A2A and needed approximately 400 lines of wrapper code beyond the SDK.
Eon's blocking A2A message/send calls failed through the gateway at a 60-second timeout although they worked locally; switching to message/stream with incremental task-status events fixed it.
In Eon's A2A deployment, content-free remote error events disappeared when the framework assembled context, leaving the orchestrator to answer without the specialist.
Eon's A2A conversations failed after roughly twenty minutes because the specialist accumulated history under context_id; Eon added an epoch counter to start fresh remote contexts.
Eon encoded app/user/session into the A2A context_id so the remote agent could use the caller's own token for catalog access; the authors warn this works only because they control both ends.
Anthropic reports 58 tools across five MCP servers consuming approximately 55,000 tokens before conversation starts, with tool definitions seen reaching 134,000 tokens.
Anthropic reports Tool Search reduced token usage by 85% and raised internal MCP-evaluation accuracy from 49% to 74% for Opus 4 and from 79.5% to 88.1% for Opus 4.5.
Anthropic's code-execution-with-MCP design exposes MCP tools as files and runs tool-using code outside the model context, cutting an example from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens (98.7% reduction).
Block/Square exposes more than 30 APIs and 200 endpoints through just three MCP tools, separating discovery, planning and execution.
Grab reports 500+ services on its internal agent framework and 50+ registered remote MCP servers, with runtime tool discovery letting new servers extend agents without redeploying them.
Spotify reported 1,500+ agent-generated PRs merged into production via its Honk background coding agent, with 60–90% time savings on the migrations discussed.
Windsurf's Cascade documents a maximum of 100 tools accessible at one time, with per-tool enable/disable controls.
A April 2025 Cursor staff response distinguished a 40-tool warning/performance threshold from an 80-tool actual limit.

The MCP 28 July 2026 authorization spec requires clients to send the resource parameter in authorization and token requests, and servers to validate that access tokens were issued for them; PKCE is mandatory.

MCP security guidance prohibits token passthrough and describes a proxy confused-deputy attack combining a static upstream client ID, dynamically registered clients and a consent cookie, defended by per-client consent and exact redirect validation.
The July 2026 MCP spec deprecates Dynamic Client Registration for new implementations in favor of pre-registration or Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD), keeping DCR as a fallback.

The MCP Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension was announced stable on 18 June 2026 and is being adopted by Anthropic, Microsoft and Okta, using identity-provider assertions to manage server access centrally.

Invariant Labs demonstrated tool poisoning (1 April 2025): malicious instructions in MCP tool descriptions visible to the model can induce unintended reads or exfiltration, plus rug pulls and cross-server shadowing; no production victim count was reported.

Invariant Labs showed in a controlled experiment (26 May 2025) that a malicious public GitHub issue could induce an agent to read private repositories and leak them in a public pull request, framed as an architectural trust/dataflow problem.

Asana's beta MCP server had a tenant-isolation bug identified 4 June 2025 that could expose another organization's data; the server was disabled 5–17 June and Asana reported no evidence of actual exploitation.
CVE-2025-6514 in mcp-remote (versions 0.0.5–0.1.15, fixed in 0.1.16) allowed command injection through an untrusted server's OAuth authorization_endpoint.
The impersonating postmark-mcp package built trust over fifteen versions, then added a backdoor in 1.0.16 that secretly BCC'd outbound email to an external address.

AgentCore Gateway permits at most one REQUEST and one RESPONSE interceptor per gateway; request headers are withheld unless passRequestHeaders is enabled, and interceptors should be idempotent due to retries.
The official MCP Registry moderation policy describes a permissive service with minimal-to-no moderation, so a registry listing is not security certification.
Google's documentation states externally hosted A2A agents registered via that route do not traverse Agent Gateway, so Agent Gateway policies do not apply to that traffic.
